normativeRubric: 1962 Ritus servandus, accessed through an English translation. Original printed Latin authority remains controlling.
globalRules: No new 1962 Mass Latin text or actor events
An anchor at words of Consecration is not an elevation event
A priest rubric is not automatically a faithful obligation
The selected form/Proper controls omissions and prayers
No correction candidate replaces the historic text without editorial acceptance
Do not merge an outdated reader-dom onto newer main

records.previousShort: The priest begins the prayers at the foot of the altar. Remain recollected and follow the opening prayer sequence if you wish.
records.proposedShort: The priest begins the prayers at the foot of the altar. Remain recollected and follow the opening prayer sequence if you wish.

records.previousShort: The preparatory prayers continue at the foot of the altar. The Confiteor and the visible striking of the breast are the next clear landmarks.
records.proposedShort: The preparatory prayers continue at the foot of the altar. The Confiteor and the visible striking of the breast are the next clear landmarks.
records.sourceLatinOpening: S. Iúdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso érue me.

records.normativeRitusSection: Ritus III.12/XIII.1—Psalm 42 omitted in certain forms

records.previousShort: The Confiteor sequence is ending. Watch for the priest to leave the foot of the altar and ascend the steps.
records.proposedShort: The celebrant strikes his breast during his own Confiteor at these words. The preparatory prayers continue; the altar ascent is not yet taking place.
records.sourceLatinOpening: S. mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa.
records.sourceComparison: C0017 is inside the priest's Confiteor, not the end of the complete preparatory sequence.
records.normativeRitusSection: III: Prayers at foot of altar

records.previousShort: The priest ascends the altar and says the quiet altar prayers. Watch for him to move to the Epistle side for the Introit.
records.proposedShort: The priest ascends the altar and says the quiet altar prayers. Watch for him to move to the Epistle side for the Introit.

records.proposedShort: The Introit begins the Proper of the Mass. Follow the text if you wish; the Kyrie and the priest’s movement toward the centre come next.

records.previousShort: Major Ordinary landmark. Watch next for Priest turns/says Dominus vobiscum, then goes to Epistle side for Collect.
records.proposedShort: At Low Mass the priest recites the Gloria if prescribed. Follow the prayer through its end; there is no separate Schola clock.

records.previousShort: Opening oration. Watch next for Epistle begins with priest still at Epistle side.
records.proposedShort: The priest says Dóminus vobíscum and the server responds before the Collect. The actual prayer follows at the Epistle side.
records.sourceLatinOpening: ℣. Dóminus vobíscum.
records.sourceComparison: C0070 is the greeting, not the proper Collect itself.

records.previousShort: Offertory is ending; Secret follows. Watch next for Quiet follows as Secret begins.
records.proposedShort: The priest turns toward the faithful for Oráte, fratres, completes the invitation quietly, and receives the server's response. The Secret prayer follows.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Oráte, fratres:
records.sourceComparison: C0130 is the start of the prayer invitation; old short text is tautological.

records.previousShort: Secret is not an audible navigation text/chant. Watch next for Public Per ómnia sæcula sæculórum / Amen, then Preface dialogue.
records.proposedShort: The priest says the Secret prayer quietly. Its conclusion leads into the audible Preface dialogue; the prayer text is supplied by the selected Mass.
records.sourceComparison: C0134 is a proper-controlled secret slot, not an independent audible text.

records.proposedShort: One of the strongest auditory landmarks. Watch next for Sanctus begins; altar bell may sound.

records.previousShort: Canon is about to begin. Watch next for Sudden drop into silence / Canon + pre-Consecration warning.
records.proposedShort: The priest says the Sanctus, then continues into the Canon quietly. The server's warning bell precedes the Consecration.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dóminus, Deus Sábaoth.
records.sourceComparison: Source rightly distinguishes audible Sanctus from secret Canon, but the original metaphorical transition is imprecise.
records.normativeRitusSection: VII.8; VIII.6

records.previousShort: Silent Canon underway. Watch next for Warning bell shortly before Consecration.
records.proposedShort: Silent Canon underway. Watch next for Warning bell shortly before Consecration.

records.previousShort: Consecration is imminent; remain kneeling/recollected. Watch next for Host elevation bells.
records.proposedShort: At Hanc igitur the Canon is still being said quietly. The Consecration approaches; follow the posture established for the congregation.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Hanc igitur oblatiónem servitutis nostræ, sed et cunctae famíliæ tuæ, quaesumus, Dómine, ut placátus accípias: diésque nostros in tua pace dispónas, atque ab æt
records.sourceComparison: The old instruction to remain kneeling cannot be inferred as a universal lay posture from the priest's rubric.
records.normativeRitusSection: VIII.4–6

records.previousShort: You are exactly at the elevation of the Sacred Host. Watch next for Chalice elevation bell after the intervening consecration.
records.proposedShort: The priest quietly pronounces the words HOC EST ENIM CORPUS MEUM. Afterward he genuflects, elevates the Sacred Host, replaces It, and genuflects again.
records.sourceLatinOpening: HOC EST ENIM CORPUS MEUM.
records.sourceComparison: C0173 is the consecratory words; the Host elevation is a subsequent separate event C0174.
records.normativeRitusSection: VIII.5–6

records.previousShort: You are exactly at the elevation of the Precious Blood. Watch next for Canon returns to silence; later Nobis quoque can become audible.
records.proposedShort: The priest quietly pronounces the words of Consecration over the chalice. After Hæc quotiescumque and a genuflection, he elevates the Chalice.
records.sourceLatinOpening: HIC EST ENIM CALIX SÁNGUINIS MEI, NOVI ET ÆTÉRNI TESTAMÉNTI: MYSTÉRIUM FÍDEI: QUI PRO VOBIS ET PRO MULTIS EFFUNDÉTUR IN REMISSIÓNEM PECCATÓRUM.
records.sourceComparison: C0179 is within the Consecration; the Chalice elevation is a subsequent separate event C0181.
records.normativeRitusSection: VIII.7

records.previousShort: Useful mid/late-Canon landmark. Watch next for Public Per omnia at the end of Canon.
records.proposedShort: At Nobis quoque peccatoribus the priest raises his voice slightly and strikes his own breast once, then continues the Canon quietly.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Nobis quoque peccatóribus
records.sourceComparison: Ritus servandus IX.3 prescribes the priest's gesture and voice, not a faithful posture cue.
records.normativeRitusSection: IX.3

records.previousShort: Canon has ended; Communion rites begin. Watch next for Pax Domini / Agnus Dei.
records.proposedShort: The Canon is approaching its concluding doxology, Per ipsum. The concluding response precedes the Lord's Prayer.
records.sourceLatinOpening: [UNCOVERS CHALICE — GENUFLECTS — TAKES SACRED HOST]
records.sourceComparison: C0201 is the action introducing Per ipsum; the Canon has not ended at this cue.

records.previousShort: Communion preparation. Watch next for Communion warning bell if faithful will receive.
records.proposedShort: At this cue the priest is praying Líbera nos. The Fraction, Pax Dómini and Agnus Dei follow; Communion of the faithful is a separate conditional stage.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Líbera nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, ab ómnibus malis, prætéritis, præséntibus et futúris: et intercedénte beáta et gloriósa semper Vírgine Dei Genetríce María, cum be
records.sourceComparison: C0212 is Libera nos, not yet the Agnus Dei; the old text skips the intervening actions.

records.previousShort: Communicants prepare/approach when directed. Watch next for Ecce Agnus Dei facing the people.
records.proposedShort: If faithful are to communicate at Mass, the server gives a warning bell shortly beforehand. This is a conditional ceremonial signal, not a fixed spoken prayer.
records.sourceComparison: Ritus servandus X.6 explicitly prescribes the minister's conditional warning; calling it merely a local custom understates the source.

records.previousShort: Faithful Communion rite is beginning. Watch next for Actual distribution at rail.
records.proposedShort: Faithful Communion rite is beginning. Watch next for Actual distribution at rail.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccáta mundi.
records.sourceComparison: Actual communicants required; second Confiteor is not a universal 1962 stage
records.normativeRitusSection: Actual communicants required; second Confiteor is not a universal 1962 stage

records.previousShort: Distribution is in progress. Watch next for Priest returns to altar and begins ablutions.
records.proposedShort: Distribution is in progress. Watch next for Priest returns to altar and begins ablutions.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Corpus ✠ Dómini nostri Iesu Christi custódiat ánimam tuam in vitam ætérnam. Amen.
records.sourceComparison: Distribution exists only if faithful actually communicate
records.normativeRitusSection: Distribution exists only if faithful actually communicate

records.previousShort: Communion section is closing. Watch next for Dóminus vobíscum before Postcommunion.
records.proposedShort: Communion section is closing. Watch next for Dóminus vobíscum before Postcommunion.
records.sourceLatinOpening: Quod ore súmpsimus, Dómine, pura mente capiámus: et de múnere temporáli fiat nobis remédium sempitérnum.
records.sourceComparison: COMMUNION Proper belongs to selected Mass; ablutions have own prayer text
records.normativeRitusSection: COMMUNION Proper belongs to selected Mass; ablutions have own prayer text

records.previousShort: Closing prayer. Watch next for Final Dóminus vobíscum / dismissal.
records.proposedShort: The priest says Dóminus vobíscum before the Postcommunion prayer or prayers. The concluding dismissal follows.
records.sourceLatinOpening: ℣. Dóminus vobíscum.
records.sourceComparison: C0251 is the greeting before the Postcommunion, not the text of the prayer itself.
records.normativeRitusSection: XI.1

records.previousShort: Mass is reaching formal conclusion. Watch next for Blessing if the rite includes it.
records.proposedShort: At this cue the priest says Ite, missa est, in a Mass for which that dismissal is appointed. Other permitted forms have a different text.
records.sourceLatinOpening: ℣. Ite, missa est.
records.sourceComparison: C0259 explicitly contains Ite, missa est; Requiem and Benedicamus variants must not inherit the same words.
records.normativeRitusSection: XI.1; XIII.1

records.previousShort: Kneel/sign yourself according to established practice. Watch next for Priest moves to Gospel side for Last Gospel if present.
records.proposedShort: When the blessing is prescribed, the priest gives it after the Placeat. The people's posture is a separate local or participation matter.
records.sourceLatinOpening: [ELEVATES EYES AND HANDS — JOINS HANDS — INCLINES HEAD TO THE CROSS]
records.sourceComparison: The previous direction to kneel/sign oneself cannot be presented as a universal lay rubric; the blessing is omitted after Benedicamus or Requiescant.
records.normativeRitusSection: XII.4

records.previousShort: Last major landmark. Watch next for Priest leaves altar / recessional.
records.proposedShort: If prescribed, the priest reads the Last Gospel, ordinarily the Prologue of St John. It is omitted when the applicable rubrics require.
records.sourceLatinOpening: ℣. Dóminus vobíscum.
records.sourceComparison: The Last Gospel is conditional; its opening cue is a greeting, and it must not be added to omitted-continuation forms.
records.normativeRitusSection: XII.4–5; XIII.1
